GTK Cyber K-Means is affected by the scale of every feature.

GTK Cyber Feature Scaling For k-means clustering, features must be scaled to the same ranges of values to contribute "equally" to the euclidean distance calculation. Each row is transformed per-column by: • Subtracting from the element in each row the mean for each feature (column) and then taking this value and • Dividing by that feature's (column's) standard deviation.

GTK Cyber Evaluating your Model The Silhouette Coefficient is a common metric for evaluating clustering "performance" in situations when the "true" cluster assignments are not known. b = mean distance to next nearest cluster a = mean distance to other points in cluster silhouette_coeff = (b - a) / max(a,b)

GTK Cyber Other uses of unsupervised learning: Dimensionality Reduction

GTK Cyber Other uses of unsupervised learning: Dimensionality Reduction • Dimensionality reduction reduces the number of features in a dataset without losing the information in a data set • Common technique: Principal Component Analysis (PCA)

GTK Cyber Other uses of unsupervised learning: Dimensionality Reduction • PCA attempts to combine the highly correlated features and represent this data with a smaller number of linearly uncorrelated features. • The algorithm keeps performing this correlation reduction, finding the directions of maximum variance in the original high dimensional data and projecting them onto a smaller dimensional space. • These newly derived components are known as principal components.

GTK Cyber PCA Example from sklearn.decomposition import PCA n_components = 784 whiten = False pca = PCA(n_components=n_components, whiten=whiten) features_train_PCA = pca.fit_transform(features_train_PCA) features_train_PCA = pd.DataFrame(data= features_train_PCA, index=train_index) print("Variance Explained by all 784 principal components: ", \ sum(pca.explained_variance_ratio_)) https://github.com/aapatel09/handson-unsupervised-learning/blob/master/03_dimensionality_reduction.ipynb The variance of all features is 1.0 (everything)

GTK Cyber PCA Example Variance Captured by First 10 Principal Components: [0.48876238] Variance Captured by First 20 Principal Components: [0.64398025] Variance Captured by First 50 Principal Components: [0.8248609] Variance Captured by First 100 Principal Components: [0.91465857] Variance Captured by First 200 Principal Components: [0.96650076] Variance Captured by First 300 Principal Components: [0.9862489] https://github.com/aapatel09/handson-unsupervised-learning/blob/master/03_dimensionality_reduction.ipynb Bottom line: 98% of the information is contained in 300 features. You can therefore, reduce the size of your dataset by half, theoretically without significantly reducing performance.
